beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: The server holds the link; a pane holds the lease
beats.body: The Archboard server's thread link names one workhorse, whichever pane speaks. The pane holding the lease sends its typed message straight to that thread as a turn or a steer, and edits the thread's queue. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations instead, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread, not a second mouth
beats.body: The coordinator is its own thread with its own model and settings, and the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorse and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse through the four operations.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach the workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made is injected into the linked workhorse's history as one developer message, after the child, epoch, link and cursor are checked again, and starts no turn. It settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried or sent anywhere else.

beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: Each tab holds its own link and lease
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own thread link and its own lease. The tab's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse, which the link then names. The pane that holds the tab's lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits the thread's queue. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations instead, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread, not a second mouth
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorse and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse through the four operations. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach each workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made goes into the history of each live tab session's workhorse as one developer message, after the child, epoch, that session's link and cursor are checked again. It starts no turn. Each delivery settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried.

beats.heading: Each thread belongs to one tab session
beats.body: The tab sessions know which session owns each thread. A notification or tool call from a thread goes to that session alone, and an approval goes to the panes of that session, so one tab's news and approvals never reach another tab. A notification for a thread that no session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

beats.heading: A tab session ends 60 seconds after its last pane closes
beats.body: Every pane names its tab when its socket opens. When no pane of the tab comes back for 60 seconds, the session ends: its lease and link go, its pending approvals are cancelled, voice and board news stop, and each of its threads is unsubscribed once no turn runs on it, so Codex unloads it. A reload within that time keeps the conversation and its approvals. When the child exits, every session is dropped, and a tab's next message starts a new workhorse.

beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: Each tab holds its own link and lease
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own thread link and its own lease. The tab's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse, which the link then names. The pane that holds the tab's lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits the thread's queue. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations instead, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread, not a second mouth
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorse and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse through the four operations. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach each workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made goes into the history of each live tab session's workhorse as one developer message, after the child, epoch, that session's link and cursor are checked again. It starts no turn. Each delivery settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried.

beats.heading: Each thread belongs to one tab session
beats.body: The tab sessions know which session owns each thread. A notification or tool call from a thread goes to that session alone, and an approval goes to the panes of that session, so one tab's news and approvals never reach another tab. A notification for a thread that no session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

beats.heading: A tab session ends 60 seconds after its last pane closes
beats.body: Every pane names its tab when its socket opens. When no pane of the tab comes back for 60 seconds, the session ends: its lease and link go, its pending approvals are cancelled, voice and board news stop, and each of its threads is unsubscribed once no turn runs on it, so Codex unloads it. A reload within that time keeps the conversation and its approvals. When the child exits, every session is dropped, and a tab's next message starts a new workhorse.

beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: Each tab holds its own link and lease
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own thread link and its own lease. The tab's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse, which the link then names. The pane that holds the tab's lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits the thread's queue. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations instead, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread, not a second mouth
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorse and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse through the four operations. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach each workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made goes into the history of each live tab session's workhorse as one developer message, after the child, epoch, that session's link and cursor are checked again. It starts no turn. Each delivery settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried.

beats.heading: Each thread belongs to one tab session
beats.body: The tab sessions know which session owns each thread. A notification or tool call from a thread goes to that session alone, and an approval goes to the panes of that session, so one tab's news and approvals never reach another tab. A notification for a thread that no session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

beats.heading: A tab session ends 60 seconds after its last pane closes
beats.body: Every pane names its tab when its socket opens. When no pane of the tab comes back for 60 seconds, the session ends: its lease and link go, its pending approvals are cancelled, voice and board news stop, and each of its threads is unsubscribed once no turn runs on it, so Codex unloads it. A reload within that time keeps the conversation and its approvals. When the child exits, every session is dropped, and a tab's next message starts a new workhorse.

beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: Each tab holds its own link and lease
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own thread link and its own lease. The tab's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse, which the link then names. The pane that holds the tab's lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits the thread's queue. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations instead, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread, not a second mouth
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorse and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse through the four operations. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach each workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made goes into the history of each live tab session's workhorse as one developer message, after the child, epoch, that session's link and cursor are checked again. It starts no turn. Each delivery settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried.

beats.heading: Each thread belongs to one tab session
beats.body: The tab sessions know which session owns each thread. A notification or tool call from a thread goes to that session alone, and an approval goes to the panes of that session, so one tab's news and approvals never reach another tab. A notification for a thread that no session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

beats.heading: A tab session ends 60 seconds after its last pane closes
beats.body: Every pane names its tab when its socket opens. When no pane of the tab comes back for 60 seconds, the session ends: its lease and link go, its pending approvals are cancelled, voice and board news stop, and each of its threads is unsubscribed once no turn runs on it, so Codex unloads it. A reload within that time keeps the conversation and its approvals. When the child exits, every session is dropped, and a tab's next message starts a new workhorse.

beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: Each tab holds its own link and lease
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own thread link and its own lease. The tab's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse, which the link then names. The pane that holds the tab's lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits the thread's queue. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations instead, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread, not a second mouth
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorse and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse through the four operations. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach each workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made goes into the history of each live tab session's workhorse as one developer message, after the child, epoch, that session's link and cursor are checked again. It starts no turn. Each delivery settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried.

beats.heading: Each thread belongs to one tab session
beats.body: The tab sessions know which session owns each thread. A notification or tool call from a thread goes to that session alone, and an approval goes to the panes of that session, so one tab's news and approvals never reach another tab. A notification for a thread that no session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

beats.heading: A tab session ends 60 seconds after its last pane closes
beats.body: Every pane names its tab when its socket opens. When no pane of the tab comes back for 60 seconds, the session ends: its lease and link go, its pending approvals are cancelled, voice and board news stop, and each of its threads is unsubscribed once no turn runs on it, so Codex unloads it. A reload within that time keeps the conversation and its approvals. When the child exits, every session is dropped, and a tab's next message starts a new workhorse.

beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: A tab holds one coordinator and a workhorse for each checkout
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own lease and its own coordinator. A pane's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse of the checkout that pane shows, which that checkout's link then names. The pane that holds the lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits that thread's queue. A pane that moves to another checkout reaches the workhorse there instead. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread that works in no checkout
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It runs in a directory of its own that holds no vault, so every command it runs names its checkout with -C. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorses and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse of the checkout it names, starting that workhorse when there is none. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach each workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made goes into the history of the workhorse whose checkout holds the board, as one developer message, after the child, epoch, that workhorse's link and cursor are checked again. It starts no turn. Each delivery settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried.

beats.heading: Each thread belongs to one tab session
beats.body: The tab sessions know which session owns each thread. A notification or tool call from a thread goes to that session alone, and an approval goes to the panes of that session (a workhorse's to those of its checkout), so one tab's news and approvals never reach another tab. A notification for a thread that no session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

beats.heading: A tab session ends 60 seconds after its last pane closes
beats.body: Every pane names its tab when its socket opens. When no pane of the tab comes back for 60 seconds, the session ends: its lease and link go, its pending approvals are cancelled, voice and board news stop, and each of its threads is unsubscribed once no turn runs on it, so Codex unloads it. A reload within that time keeps the conversation and its approvals. When the child exits, every session is dropped, and a tab's next message starts a new workhorse.

beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: A tab holds one coordinator and a workhorse for each checkout
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own lease and its own coordinator. A pane's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse of the checkout that pane shows, which that checkout's link then names. The pane that holds the lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits that thread's queue. A pane that moves to another checkout reaches the workhorse there instead. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread that works in no checkout
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It runs in a directory of its own that holds no vault, so every command it runs names its checkout with -C. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorses and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse of the checkout it names, starting that workhorse when there is none. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach each workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made goes into the history of the workhorse whose checkout holds the board, as one developer message, after the child, epoch, that workhorse's link and cursor are checked again. It starts no turn. Each delivery settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried.

beats.heading: Each thread belongs to one tab session
beats.body: The tab sessions know which session owns each thread. A notification or tool call from a thread goes to that session alone, and an approval goes to the panes of that session (a workhorse's to those of its checkout), so one tab's news and approvals never reach another tab. A notification for a thread that no session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

beats.heading: A tab session ends 60 seconds after its last pane closes
beats.body: Every pane names its tab when its socket opens. When no pane of the tab comes back for 60 seconds, the session ends: its lease and link go, its pending approvals are cancelled, voice and board news stop, and each of its threads is unsubscribed once no turn runs on it, so Codex unloads it. A reload within that time keeps the conversation and its approvals. When the child exits, every session is dropped, and a tab's next message starts a new workhorse.

nodes.name: Generation composition
nodes.responsibility: Starts the private child, then builds each generation's object graph over a transport and identity ledger that outlive it
nodes.description: installProductionCodexWorkbench hands the owner lifecycle createCodexProcess and a generation factory. The factories (codex-workbench-factories.ts) build the components in the order they depend on each other, the gateway last. codex-workbench-session-factories.ts builds one tab session's owners when the tab sessions open it. A child's exit drops every tab session, and nothing is resumed.

nodes.name: Browser gateway
nodes.responsibility: The one door a browser has into the workbench: snapshots out, admitted commands in, one lease per tab session, and every pane of a tab is carried out by the workhorse of the checkout the tab shows
nodes.description: The gateway asks which checkout the pane's tab shows on every read and command, because the person can activate another one at any time. It hears the change and presents every pane of the tab again, with the workhorse of the new checkout. A lease taken before a switch is refused as link_changed. A command runs on the workhorse its lease was claimed for, and once it has run only that workhorse's own link is asked whether it still stands, so a switch meanwhile does not make its outcome unknown. A workhorse's approval terminal is retired once the panes that show its checkout have shown it, and a coordinator's once every pane of the tab has.

nodes.name: Codex process
nodes.responsibility: Owns the child: proves the executable, prepares the Codex home every Archboard server on the machine shares, spawns the child in the coordinator's directory and reaps its group
nodes.description: One Archboard-only CODEX_HOME and SQLite home under the state directory serve every server on the machine, so one sign-in serves them all; each server keeps its own owner lock and epoch ledger under its port. Its config.toml gets the auto-review defaults it lacks (approvals_reviewer auto_review, workspace-write sandbox with network access) and keeps whatever Codex or a person set; a config naming another SQLite home, or not TOML, is refused. The child runs in the coordinator's directory under the server's state directory, which is no checkout and holds no vault, only a link to the server's archboard skill: the coordinator thread works there, so a command it runs without -C is refused, while each workhorse thread works in its own checkout. The child's environment is a short allow-list plus the server's own URL, with auto-start off and the server's bin directory first on PATH: a thread's archboard is the server's own source in whichever checkout the thread works in, and it never starts another server. On shutdown, stdin closes first. The owner waits within a short EOF grace, then reaps every remaining group within the composed deadline.

nodes.name: Codex transport
nodes.responsibility: One newline-framed JSON object at a time each way, correlated to its request, and each tool call routed to the owner registered for its namespace
nodes.description: The versioned wire contract it decodes against lives beside it in codex-protocol. A dynamic tool call reaches the owner registered for its namespace and manifest digest: the thread tools, the coordinator tools, or tell_coordinator.

nodes.name: Codex session
nodes.responsibility: One initialized session and the reviewed methods it will send

nodes.name: Thread link
nodes.responsibility: Which workhorse each tab session and checkout is bound to, made by the first message or Talk of the pane's checkout: the binding, and the refusal when two disagree

nodes.name: Workhorse queue
nodes.responsibility: Codex's queue of messages waiting for the workhorse: list, add, edit, reorder, delete, or start one now

nodes.name: Voice coordinator
nodes.responsibility: The separate fast thread each tab session's voice attaches to, started with the tab's first message or Talk: the voice model's subconscious, which routes sustained work to a named checkout's workhorse

nodes.name: Codex app-server
nodes.responsibility: The Codex binary, run as one private child over stdio in the Archboard-only Codex home
nodes.description: Spawned as `app-server --stdio --strict-config`. Its threads are each tab session's coordinator and one workhorse for each checkout, and every thread runs in its auto-review mode. Nothing here describes its internals.

nodes.name: Browser pane
nodes.responsibility: The pane a user works in: it names its tab session, holds the tab's lease, sends commands and draws the published state

nodes.name: Epoch ledger
nodes.responsibility: Which child generation owns which thread, on disk, with staged operations that commit or roll back

nodes.name: Workhorse operations
nodes.responsibility: The four things the coordinator may ask of the workhorse of a checkout it names, one at a time: delegate, steer, inspect, manage its queue; each workhorse has its own

nodes.name: Realtime voice
nodes.responsibility: Starts the realtime leg on the coordinator's thread, hands a narrated walkthrough's steps to the voice model, and carries its transcript back
nodes.description: Archboard never speaks to a voice endpoint itself: the child brokers it, and the media travels browser to provider over the peer connection the tab made.

nodes.name: Approvals
nodes.responsibility: Every approval the child raises: staged, published to the tab session whose thread asked, answered exactly once, settled
nodes.description: An approval from a thread that no live tab session owns is cancelled when it arrives. A reload within the grace keeps a tab session's pending approvals, and the end of the session cancels them. A workhorse's approval is shown to the panes of its tab that show its checkout, and the coordinator's to every pane of its tab session.

nodes.name: Thread tool calls
nodes.responsibility: The archboard_app tools a thread calls on the server's other threads: list, read, create, fork, message, wait
nodes.description: A creation, fork or message runs only once the user approves it in a pane of the calling thread's tab session, under the generation that may act. A thread it creates or forks works in the checkout of its caller.

nodes.name: Coordinator callbacks
nodes.responsibility: While voice is live, workhorse news for the coordinator, naming the checkout of its workhorse, and pane news for the voice model, each once and in order

nodes.name: Board-change delivery
nodes.responsibility: Tells each workhorse what a user changed on the boards of its checkout: one quiet developer message, settled once
nodes.description: Before each delivery it checks the child, epoch, thread link and cursor again; the outcome is delivered, not delivered with a reason, or unknown, and it is never retried.

nodes.name: Semantic context
nodes.responsibility: One per tab session for voice and one per workhorse for the boards of its checkout: turns the panes' gestures and every settled board change into briefs and events
nodes.description: Each brief names its board's vault, so a thread passes it to the CLI with -C. The voice side hears the board changes of the vaults its tab session's panes are in, and a workhorse hears only those of the vaults in its own checkout, so it is told about the boards it works on.

nodes.name: Tab sessions
nodes.responsibility: What each browser tab owns: its coordinator and voice, and one workhorse for each checkout it works in, found by the thread a notification or tool call names
nodes.description: One record per tab session, opened when a pane socket of the tab connects and built by codex-workbench-session-factories.ts. The coordinator, voice, spoken approval, coordinator tools and callbacks are the tab's; the workhorses are built on first use, one for each checkout. A notification goes to the session that owns its thread, or to every session when no session owns the thread yet, and a workhorse thread belongs to its workhorse. A tool call from a thread that no session owns is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody. It notes the conversation shown when each coordinator turn starts and the work each workhorse's operations give. When a session ends, every link is cleared, its approvals are cancelled, its voice and board news stop, and its threads are unsubscribed once no turn runs on them.

nodes.name: Tab session presence
nodes.responsibility: Knows which browser tab each pane on screen belongs to, which checkout's conversation the tab shows, and ends a tab session when no pane of it comes back within 60 seconds
nodes.description: It lives as long as the server process, not as long as one child. A pane of the tab that comes back within the grace cancels the end, so a reload keeps the conversation. The shown checkout is pinned on the first read to the checkout of the tab's focused pane, else of the pane that asked, and only the person's own act in the page changes it, through the activation route: an agent's browser show never does, so the dock never moves while somebody types. It ends with the tab.

nodes.name: Conversation start
nodes.responsibility: Starts a conversation on a pane's first message or Talk: the tab's coordinator ready first, then the workhorse of the shown checkout, then board news to it
nodes.description: A coordinator that cannot start refuses the message or Talk with its reason, and no workhorse starts. New conversation replaces the workhorse of the shown checkout only and keeps the tab's coordinator, which speaks for every workhorse of the tab. The old workhorse thread is given up and Codex unloads it once no turn runs on it. A delegation to a checkout whose workhorse has no thread that can run turns starts that thread the same way, but leaves the coordinator alone: it is running the turn that gives the work.

nodes.name: Workhorse start
nodes.responsibility: Opens the thread one workhorse's link will name, with its instructions and both tool manifests, under a staged epoch operation

nodes.name: Thread unload
nodes.responsibility: Unsubscribes a thread once no turn and no voice session runs on it, so Codex unloads it
nodes.description: It reads the thread's status first, then follows the child's notifications until the thread is idle and its voice session has closed. The thread keeps its history on disk either way. The module is reached through createCodexThreadUnload from its root; the returned unload method implements this responsibility.

nodes.name: Session workhorses
nodes.responsibility: One workhorse for each checkout of a tab session: its starter, board news, queue, operations and link actions, built on first use
nodes.description: A workhorse works in its checkout, the directory that holds its vault, so it reads that repository's AGENTS.md, skills and Codex configuration. Its thread-link key is the tab session and the checkout together. It belongs to the checkout, not to the repository identity, so a new chosen checkout leaves it linked. noteActiveTurn keeps the turn running on a workhorse from turn/started on its current thread to the turn/completed of the thread the turn started on, which New conversation may have left meanwhile, and stopWorkhorses interrupts that turn for one checkout or for every workhorse of the tab. The coordinator's stop_workhorses tool stops every running workhorse of its tab session by voice.

nodes.name: Workhorse checkouts
nodes.responsibility: Names the checkout a coordinator call gives work to, and starts that checkout's workhorse when a delegation finds none
nodes.description: The checkout a path names is the directory that holds the vault the path resolves to, by real path and in the layout the server serves: a directory that holds a .archboard/vault, or the directory that holds a vault the path is. So a checkout reached through a link, and a vault that is itself a link, name the checkout of the pane in it; a vault whose link leads out of the layout names none. Of the coordinator's tools only a delegation starts a workhorse; the other three refuse a checkout that has none. A workhorse that cannot be built or started, because its tab has gone, leaves the delegation to refuse, so the coordinator's turn is always answered.

nodes.name: Workhorse list
nodes.responsibility: Lists the tab session's live workhorses by repository and checkout, with the shown one and a mark for each that waits for an approval or for the person
nodes.description: The shown checkout is listed even before its first message, as not live, because a typed message goes there. A workhorse is live once its start has a thread. The list is bounded so a snapshot always fits the browser contract, and it is read into the owner projection that every pane of the tab receives.

nodes.name: Coordinator turn homes
nodes.responsibility: Remembers, for each coordinator turn, the conversation shown when it started and the checkouts it gave work to, so the dock shows the turn in the right conversation
nodes.description: A turn that delivered, steered or queued work, or whose delivery may have reached the workhorse, shows in the conversation of each workhorse it reached. A delegation the workhorse refused as busy or with an invalid body gave it nothing, and moves the turn nowhere. A turn that gave work to none shows in the conversation shown while it ran. A turn with no record shows in whatever conversation is shown. The timeline keeps only the turns of the shown conversation before it spends its budget.

nodes.name: Child ownership
nodes.responsibility: Owns the private Codex child and what outlives each generation of it: the process, the transport, the protocol session, the ledger of which generation owns a thread, and unloading idle threads

nodes.name: Per-tab sessions
nodes.responsibility: Gives each browser tab its own session: finds the session a call names, knows which tab each pane belongs to, ends a tab no pane returns to, and remembers where each coordinator turn is shown

The factories (codex-workbench-factories.ts) build the components in the order they depend on each other, the gateway last. codex-workbench-session-factories.ts builds one tab session's owners when the tab sessions open it. A child's exit drops every tab session, and nothing is resumed.

nodes.name: Browser gateway
nodes.responsibility: The one door a browser has into the workbench: snapshots out, admitted commands in, one lease per tab session, and every pane of a tab is carried out by the workhorse of the checkout the tab shows
nodes.description: The gateway asks which checkout the pane's tab shows on every read and command, because the person can activate another one at any time. It hears the change and presents every pane of the tab again, with the workhorse of the new checkout. A lease taken before a switch is refused as link_changed. A command runs on the workhorse its lease was claimed for, and once it has run only that workhorse's own link is asked whether it still stands, so a switch meanwhile does not make its outcome unknown. A workhorse's approval terminal is retired once the panes that show its checkout have shown it, and a coordinator's once every pane of the tab has.

nodes.name: Codex process
nodes.responsibility: Owns the child: proves the executable, prepares the Codex home every Archboard server on the machine shares, spawns the child in the coordinator's directory and reaps its group
nodes.description: One Archboard-only CODEX_HOME and SQLite home under the state directory serve every server on the machine, so one sign-in serves them all; each server keeps its own owner lock and epoch ledger under its port. Its config.toml gets the auto-review defaults it lacks (approvals_reviewer auto_review, workspace-write sandbox with network access) and keeps whatever Codex or a person set; a config naming another SQLite home, or not TOML, is refused. The child runs in the coordinator's directory under the server's state directory, which is no checkout and holds no vault, only a link to the server's archboard skill: the coordinator thread works there, so a command it runs without -C is refused, while each workhorse thread works in its own checkout. The child's environment is a short allow-list plus the server's own URL, with auto-start off and the server's bin directory first on PATH: a thread's archboard is the server's own source in whichever checkout the thread works in, and it never starts another server. On shutdown, stdin closes first. The owner waits within a short EOF grace, then reaps every remaining group within the composed deadline.

nodes.name: Codex transport
nodes.responsibility: One newline-framed JSON object at a time each way, correlated to its request, and each tool call routed to the owner registered for its namespace
nodes.description: The versioned wire contract it decodes against lives beside it in codex-protocol. A dynamic tool call reaches the owner registered for its namespace and manifest digest: the thread tools, the coordinator tools, or tell_coordinator.

nodes.name: Codex session
nodes.responsibility: One initialized session and the reviewed methods it will send

nodes.name: Thread link
nodes.responsibility: Which workhorse each tab session and checkout is bound to, made by the first message or Talk of the pane's checkout: the binding, and the refusal when two disagree

nodes.name: Workhorse queue
nodes.responsibility: Codex's queue of messages waiting for the workhorse: list, add, edit, reorder, delete, or start one now

nodes.name: Voice coordinator
nodes.responsibility: The separate fast thread each tab session's voice attaches to, started with the tab's first message or Talk: the voice model's subconscious, which routes sustained work to a named checkout's workhorse

nodes.name: Codex app-server
nodes.responsibility: The Codex binary, run as one private child over stdio in the Archboard-only Codex home
nodes.description: Spawned as `app-server --stdio --strict-config`. Its threads are each tab session's coordinator and one workhorse for each checkout, and every thread runs in its auto-review mode. Nothing here describes its internals.

nodes.name: Browser pane
nodes.responsibility: The pane a user works in: it names its tab session, holds the tab's lease, sends commands and draws the published state

nodes.name: Epoch ledger
nodes.responsibility: Which child generation owns which thread, on disk, with staged operations that commit or roll back

nodes.name: Workhorse operations
nodes.responsibility: The four things the coordinator may ask of the workhorse of a checkout it names, one at a time: delegate, steer, inspect, manage its queue; each workhorse has its own

nodes.name: Realtime voice
nodes.responsibility: Starts the realtime leg on the coordinator's thread, hands a narrated walkthrough's steps to the voice model, and carries its transcript back
nodes.description: Archboard never speaks to a voice endpoint itself: the child brokers it, and the media travels browser to provider over the peer connection the tab made.

nodes.name: Approvals
nodes.responsibility: Every approval the child raises: staged, published to the tab session whose thread asked, answered exactly once, settled
nodes.description: An approval from a thread that no live tab session owns is cancelled when it arrives. A reload within the grace keeps a tab session's pending approvals, and the end of the session cancels them. A workhorse's approval is shown to the panes of its tab that show its checkout, and the coordinator's to every pane of its tab session.

nodes.name: Thread tool calls
nodes.responsibility: The archboard_app tools a thread calls on the server's other threads: list, read, create, fork, message, wait
nodes.description: A creation, fork or message runs only once the user approves it in a pane of the calling thread's tab session, under the generation that may act. A thread it creates or forks works in the checkout of its caller.

nodes.name: Coordinator callbacks
nodes.responsibility: While voice is live, workhorse news for the coordinator, naming the checkout of its workhorse, and pane news for the voice model, each once and in order

nodes.name: Board-change delivery
nodes.responsibility: Tells each workhorse what a user changed on the boards of its checkout: one quiet developer message, settled once
nodes.description: Before each delivery it checks the child, epoch, thread link and cursor again; the outcome is delivered, not delivered with a reason, or unknown, and it is never retried.

nodes.name: Semantic context
nodes.responsibility: One per tab session for voice and one per workhorse for the boards of its checkout: turns the panes' gestures and every settled board change into briefs and events
nodes.description: Each brief names its board's vault, so a thread passes it to the CLI with -C. The voice side hears the board changes of the vaults its tab session's panes are in, and a workhorse hears only those of the vaults in its own checkout, so it is told about the boards it works on.

nodes.name: Tab sessions
nodes.responsibility: What each browser tab owns: its coordinator and voice, and one workhorse for each checkout it works in, found by the thread a notification or tool call names
nodes.description: One record per tab session, opened when a pane socket of the tab connects and built by codex-workbench-session-factories.ts. The coordinator, voice, spoken approval, coordinator tools and callbacks are the tab's; the workhorses are built on first use, one for each checkout. A notification goes to the session that owns its thread, or to every session when no session owns the thread yet, and a workhorse thread belongs to its workhorse. A tool call from a thread that no session owns is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody. It notes the conversation shown when each coordinator turn starts and the work each workhorse's operations give. When a session ends, every link is cleared, its approvals are cancelled, its voice and board news stop, and its threads are unsubscribed once no turn runs on them.

nodes.name: Tab session presence
nodes.responsibility: Knows which browser tab each pane on screen belongs to, which checkout's conversation the tab shows, and ends a tab session when no pane of it comes back within 60 seconds
nodes.description: It lives as long as the server process, not as long as one child. A pane of the tab that comes back within the grace cancels the end, so a reload keeps the conversation. The shown checkout is pinned on the first read to the checkout of the tab's focused pane, else of the pane that asked, and only the person's own act in the page changes it, through the activation route: an agent's browser show never does, so the dock never moves while somebody types. It ends with the tab.

nodes.name: Conversation start
nodes.responsibility: Starts a conversation on a pane's first message or Talk: the tab's coordinator ready first, then the workhorse of the shown checkout, then board news to it
nodes.description: A coordinator that cannot start refuses the message or Talk with its reason, and no workhorse starts. New conversation replaces the workhorse of the shown checkout only and keeps the tab's coordinator, which speaks for every workhorse of the tab. The old workhorse thread is given up and Codex unloads it once no turn runs on it. A delegation to a checkout whose workhorse has no thread that can run turns starts that thread the same way, but leaves the coordinator alone: it is running the turn that gives the work.

nodes.name: Workhorse start
nodes.responsibility: Opens the thread one workhorse's link will name, with its instructions and both tool manifests, under a staged epoch operation

nodes.name: Thread unload
nodes.responsibility: Unsubscribes a thread once no turn and no voice session runs on it, so Codex unloads it
nodes.description: It reads the thread's status first, then follows the child's notifications until the thread is idle and its voice session has closed. The thread keeps its history on disk either way. The module is reached through createCodexThreadUnload from its root; the returned unload method implements this responsibility.

nodes.name: Session workhorses
nodes.responsibility: One workhorse for each checkout of a tab session: its starter, board news, queue, operations and link actions, built on first use
nodes.description: A workhorse works in its checkout, the directory that holds its vault, so it reads that repository's AGENTS.md, skills and Codex configuration. Its thread-link key is the tab session and the checkout together. It belongs to the checkout, not to the repository identity, so a new chosen checkout leaves it linked. noteActiveTurn keeps the turn running on a workhorse from turn/started on its current thread to the turn/completed of the thread the turn started on, which New conversation may have left meanwhile, and stopWorkhorses interrupts that turn for one checkout or for every workhorse of the tab. The coordinator's stop_workhorses tool stops every running workhorse of its tab session by voice.

nodes.name: Workhorse checkouts
nodes.responsibility: Names the checkout a coordinator call gives work to, and starts that checkout's workhorse when a delegation finds none
nodes.description: The checkout a path names is the directory that holds the vault the path resolves to, by real path and in the layout the server serves: a directory that holds a .archboard/vault, or the directory that holds a vault the path is. So a checkout reached through a link, and a vault that is itself a link, name the checkout of the pane in it; a vault whose link leads out of the layout names none. Of the coordinator's tools only a delegation starts a workhorse; the other three refuse a checkout that has none. A workhorse that cannot be built or started, because its tab has gone, leaves the delegation to refuse, so the coordinator's turn is always answered.

nodes.name: Workhorse list
nodes.responsibility: Lists the tab session's live workhorses by repository and checkout, with the shown one and a mark for each that waits for an approval or for the person
nodes.description: The shown checkout is listed even before its first message, as not live, because a typed message goes there. A workhorse is live once its start has a thread. The list is bounded so a snapshot always fits the browser contract, and it is read into the owner projection that every pane of the tab receives.

nodes.name: Coordinator turn homes
nodes.responsibility: Remembers, for each coordinator turn, the conversation shown when it started and the checkouts it gave work to, so the dock shows the turn in the right conversation
nodes.description: A turn that delivered, steered or queued work, or whose delivery may have reached the workhorse, shows in the conversation of each workhorse it reached. A delegation the workhorse refused as busy or with an invalid body gave it nothing, and moves the turn nowhere. A turn that gave work to none shows in the conversation shown while it ran. A turn with no record shows in whatever conversation is shown. The timeline keeps only the turns of the shown conversation before it spends its budget.

nodes.name: Pane conversations

nodes.name: Workhorses

nodes.name: Voice

nodes.name: Command admission
nodes.responsibility: Admits a command only under its live lease, link, readiness and pending approval

nodes.name: Command dispatch
nodes.responsibility: Routes each admitted command to its account, thread, text, queue, approval or voice action

nodes.name: Typed message actions

nodes.name: Operations contract

beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: A tab holds one coordinator and a workhorse for each checkout
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own lease and its own coordinator. A pane's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse of the checkout that pane shows, which that checkout's link then names. The pane that holds the lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits that thread's queue. A pane that moves to another checkout reaches the workhorse there instead. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread that works in no checkout
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It runs in a directory of its own that holds no vault, so every command it runs names its checkout with -C. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorses and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse of the checkout it names, starting that workhorse when there is none. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach each workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made goes into the history of the workhorse whose checkout holds the board, as one developer message, after the child, epoch, that workhorse's link and cursor are checked again. It starts no turn. Each delivery settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried.

beats.heading: Each thread belongs to one tab session
beats.body: The tab sessions know which session owns each thread. A notification or tool call from a thread goes to that session alone, and an approval goes to the panes of that session (a workhorse's to those of its checkout), so one tab's news and approvals never reach another tab. A notification for a thread that no session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

beats.heading: A tab session ends 60 seconds after its last pane closes
beats.body: Every pane names its tab when its socket opens. When no pane of the tab comes back for 60 seconds, the session ends: its lease and link go, its pending approvals are cancelled, voice and board news stop, and each of its threads is unsubscribed once no turn runs on it, so Codex unloads it. A reload within that time keeps the conversation and its approvals. When the child exits, every session is dropped, and a tab's next message starts a new workhorse.

nodes.description: Inspection reads actual turns, recent progress, descendants, and pending requests. Stop clears pending requests and interrupts the proven work tree. It observes settlement and reports complete, partial, or unconfirmed results. New work waits for resolution and a fresh user request. Existing ownership and epoch records govern effects.

nodes.name: Realtime voice
nodes.responsibility: Starts the realtime leg on the coordinator's thread, hands a narrated walkthrough's steps to the voice model, and carries its transcript back
nodes.description: Archboard never speaks to a voice endpoint itself: the child brokers it, and the media travels browser to provider over the peer connection the tab made.

nodes.name: Approvals
nodes.responsibility: Every approval the child raises: staged, published to the tab session whose thread asked, answered exactly once, settled
nodes.description: An approval from a thread that no live tab session owns is cancelled when it arrives. A reload within the grace keeps a tab session's pending approvals, and the end of the session cancels them. A workhorse's approval is shown to the panes of its tab that show its checkout, and the coordinator's to every pane of its tab session.

nodes.name: Thread tool calls
nodes.responsibility: The archboard_app tools a thread calls on the server's other threads: list, read, create, fork, message, wait
nodes.description: A creation, fork or message runs only once the user approves it in a pane of the calling thread's tab session, under the generation that may act. A thread it creates or forks works in the checkout of its caller.

nodes.name: Coordinator callbacks
nodes.responsibility: While voice is live, workhorse news for the coordinator, naming the checkout of its workhorse, and pane news for the voice model, each once and in order

nodes.name: Board-change delivery
nodes.responsibility: Tells each workhorse what a user changed on the boards of its checkout: one quiet developer message, settled once
nodes.description: Before each delivery it checks the child, epoch, thread link and cursor again; the outcome is delivered, not delivered with a reason, or unknown, and it is never retried.

nodes.name: Semantic context
nodes.responsibility: One per tab session for voice and one per workhorse for the boards of its checkout: turns the panes' gestures and every settled board change into briefs and events
nodes.description: Each brief names its board's vault, so a thread passes it to the CLI with -C. The voice side hears the board changes of the vaults its tab session's panes are in, and a workhorse hears only those of the vaults in its own checkout, so it is told about the boards it works on.

nodes.name: Tab sessions
nodes.responsibility: What each browser tab owns: its coordinator and voice, and one workhorse for each checkout it works in, found by the thread a notification or tool call names
nodes.description: One record per tab session, opened when a pane socket of the tab connects and built by codex-workbench-session-factories.ts. The coordinator, voice, spoken approval, coordinator tools and callbacks are the tab's; the workhorses are built on first use, one for each checkout. A notification goes to the session that owns its thread, or to every session when no session owns the thread yet, and a workhorse thread belongs to its workhorse. A tool call from a thread that no session owns is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody. It notes the conversation shown when each coordinator turn starts and the work each workhorse's operations give. When a session ends, every link is cleared, its approvals are cancelled, its voice and board news stop, and its threads are unsubscribed once no turn runs on them.

nodes.name: Tab session presence
nodes.responsibility: Knows which browser tab each pane on screen belongs to, which checkout's conversation the tab shows, and ends a tab session when no pane of it comes back within 60 seconds
nodes.description: It lives as long as the server process, not as long as one child. A pane of the tab that comes back within the grace cancels the end, so a reload keeps the conversation. The shown checkout is pinned on the first read to the checkout of the tab's focused pane, else of the pane that asked, and only the person's own act in the page changes it, through the activation route: an agent's browser show never does, so the dock never moves while somebody types. It ends with the tab.

nodes.name: Conversation start
nodes.responsibility: Starts a conversation on a pane's first message or Talk: the tab's coordinator ready first, then the workhorse of the shown checkout, then board news to it
nodes.description: A coordinator that cannot start refuses the message or Talk with its reason, and no workhorse starts. New conversation replaces the workhorse of the shown checkout only and keeps the tab's coordinator, which speaks for every workhorse of the tab. The old workhorse thread is given up and Codex unloads it once no turn runs on it. A delegation to a checkout whose workhorse has no thread that can run turns starts that thread the same way, but leaves the coordinator alone: it is running the turn that gives the work.

nodes.name: Workhorse start
nodes.responsibility: Opens the thread one workhorse's link will name, with its instructions and both tool manifests, under a staged epoch operation

nodes.name: Thread unload
nodes.responsibility: Unsubscribes a thread once no turn and no voice session runs on it, so Codex unloads it
nodes.description: It reads the thread's status first, then follows the child's notifications until the thread is idle and its voice session has closed. The thread keeps its history on disk either way. The module is reached through createCodexThreadUnload from its root; the returned unload method implements this responsibility.

nodes.name: Session workhorses
nodes.responsibility: One workhorse for each checkout of a tab session: its starter, board news, queue, operations and link actions, built on first use
nodes.description: A workhorse works in its checkout, the directory that holds its vault, so it reads that repository's AGENTS.md, skills and Codex configuration. Its thread-link key is the tab session and the checkout together. It belongs to the checkout, not to the repository identity, so a new chosen checkout leaves it linked. noteActiveTurn keeps the turn running on a workhorse from turn/started on its current thread to the turn/completed of the thread the turn started on, which New conversation may have left meanwhile, and stopWorkhorses asks the operations of one checkout's workhorse, or of every workhorse of the tab, to stop its whole work tree. The coordinator's stop_workhorses tool stops every running workhorse of its tab session by voice.

nodes.name: Workhorse checkouts
nodes.responsibility: Names the checkout a coordinator call gives work to, and starts that checkout's workhorse when a delegation finds none
nodes.description: The checkout a path names is the directory that holds the vault the path resolves to, by real path and in the layout the server serves: a directory that holds a .archboard/vault, or the directory that holds a vault the path is. So a checkout reached through a link, and a vault that is itself a link, name the checkout of the pane in it; a vault whose link leads out of the layout names none. Of the coordinator's tools only a delegation starts a workhorse; the other three refuse a checkout that has none. A workhorse that cannot be built or started, because its tab has gone, leaves the delegation to refuse, so the coordinator's turn is always answered.

nodes.name: Workhorse list
nodes.responsibility: Lists the tab session's live workhorses by repository and checkout, with the shown one and a mark for each that waits for an approval or for the person
nodes.description: The shown checkout is listed even before its first message, as not live, because a typed message goes there. A workhorse is live once its start has a thread. The list is bounded so a snapshot always fits the browser contract, and it is read into the owner projection that every pane of the tab receives.

nodes.name: Coordinator turn homes
nodes.responsibility: Remembers, for each coordinator turn, the conversation shown when it started and the checkouts it gave work to, so the dock shows the turn in the right conversation
nodes.description: A turn that delivered, steered or queued work, or whose delivery may have reached the workhorse, shows in the conversation of each workhorse it reached. A delegation the workhorse refused as busy or with an invalid body gave it nothing, and moves the turn nowhere. A turn that gave work to none shows in the conversation shown while it ran. A turn with no record shows in whatever conversation is shown. The timeline keeps only the turns of the shown conversation before it spends its budget.

nodes.name: Child ownership
nodes.responsibility: Owns the private Codex child and what outlives each generation of it: the process, the transport, the protocol session, the ledger of which generation owns a thread, and unloading idle threads

nodes.name: Per-tab sessions
nodes.responsibility: Gives each browser tab its own session: finds the session a call names, knows which tab each pane belongs to, ends a tab no pane returns to, and remembers where each coordinator turn is shown

nodes.name: Pane conversations
nodes.responsibility: What a pane sees and says: the gateway with its lease, snapshots and commands, the start of a conversation, the dock's list of workhorses, and the approvals raised to the person

nodes.name: Workhorses
nodes.responsibility: The sustained work of each checkout: a workhorse's thread link, queue, operations, start and board news, built per tab session on first use, with its tool calls and the context of what changed

nodes.name: Voice
nodes.responsibility: The separate fast coordinator thread of a tab session, its realtime voice leg, and the callbacks that tell it and the voice model workhorse and pane news while voice is live

nodes.name: Command admission
nodes.responsibility: Admits a command only under its live lease, link, readiness and pending approval

nodes.name: Command dispatch
nodes.responsibility: Routes each admitted command to its account, thread, text, queue, approval or voice action

nodes.name: Typed message actions
nodes.responsibility: Reads the exact leased thread and starts, steers or interrupts its turn

nodes.name: Turn execution
nodes.responsibility: Implements delegation, steering, inspection and queue changes through the shared operation runtime

nodes.name: Operation validation
nodes.responsibility: Captures the current binding and classifies both linked threads around each coordinator effect

nodes.name: Operation lifecycle
nodes.responsibility: Stages operations, follows their workhorse turns and settles their outcomes once

nodes.name: Operations contract
nodes.responsibility: Defines the requests, results and notifications of the four workhorse operations

nodes.name: Start contract
nodes.responsibility: Defines the starter port that exposes thread creation and its current snapshot

nodes.name: Browser message publication
nodes.responsibility: Delivers each gateway update to its connection subscribers without one failed listener blocking the others

beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: A tab holds one coordinator and a workhorse for each checkout
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own lease and its own coordinator. A pane's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse of the checkout that pane shows, which that checkout's link then names. The pane that holds the lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits that thread's queue. A pane that moves to another checkout reaches the workhorse there instead. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread that works in no checkout
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It runs in a directory of its own that holds no vault, so every command it runs names its checkout with -C. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorses and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse of the checkout it names, starting that workhorse when there is none. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach each workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made goes into the history of the workhorse whose checkout holds the board, as one developer message, after the child, epoch, that workhorse's link and cursor are checked again. It starts no turn. Each delivery settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried.

beats.heading: Each thread belongs to one tab session
beats.body: The tab sessions know which session owns each thread. A notification or tool call from a thread goes to that session alone, and an approval goes to the panes of that session (a workhorse's to those of its checkout), so one tab's news and approvals never reach another tab. A notification for a thread that no session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

beats.heading: A tab session ends 60 seconds after its last pane closes
beats.body: Every pane names its tab when its socket opens. When no pane of the tab comes back for 60 seconds, the session ends: its lease and link go, its pending approvals are cancelled, voice and board news stop, and each of its threads is unsubscribed once no turn runs on it, so Codex unloads it. A reload within that time keeps the conversation and its approvals. When the child exits, every session is dropped, and a tab's next message starts a new workhorse.

nodes.name: Generation composition
nodes.responsibility: Starts the private child, then builds each generation's object graph over a transport and identity ledger that outlive it
nodes.description: installProductionCodexWorkbench hands the owner lifecycle createCodexProcess and a generation factory. The factories (codex-workbench-factories.ts) build the components in the order they depend on each other, the gateway last. codex-workbench-session-factories.ts builds one tab session's owners when the tab sessions open it. A child's exit drops every tab session, and nothing is resumed.

nodes.name: Browser gateway
nodes.responsibility: The one door a browser has into the workbench: snapshots out, admitted commands in, one lease per tab session, and every pane of a tab is carried out by the workhorse of the checkout the tab shows
nodes.description: The gateway asks which checkout the pane's tab shows on every read and command, because the person can activate another one at any time. It hears the change and presents every pane of the tab again, with the workhorse of the new checkout. A lease taken before a switch is refused as link_changed. A command runs on the workhorse its lease was claimed for, and once it has run only that workhorse's own link is asked whether it still stands, so a switch meanwhile does not make its outcome unknown. A workhorse's approval terminal is retired once the panes that show its checkout have shown it, and a coordinator's once every pane of the tab has.

nodes.name: Codex process
nodes.responsibility: Owns the child: proves the executable, prepares the Codex home every Archboard server on the machine shares, spawns the child in the coordinator's directory and reaps its group
nodes.description: One Archboard-only CODEX_HOME and SQLite home under the state directory serve every server on the machine, so one sign-in serves them all; each server keeps its own owner lock and epoch ledger under its port. Its config.toml gets the auto-review defaults it lacks (approvals_reviewer auto_review, workspace-write sandbox with network access) and keeps whatever Codex or a person set; a config naming another SQLite home, or not TOML, is refused. The child runs in the coordinator's directory under the server's state directory, which is no checkout and holds no vault, only a link to the server's archboard skill: the coordinator thread works there, so a command it runs without -C is refused, while each workhorse thread works in its own checkout. The child's environment is a short allow-list plus the server's own URL, with auto-start off and the server's bin directory first on PATH: a thread's archboard is the server's own source in whichever checkout the thread works in, and it never starts another server. On shutdown, stdin closes first. The owner waits within a short EOF grace, then reaps every remaining group within the composed deadline.
