nodes.name: Tab sessions
nodes.responsibility: What each browser tab owns: its coordinator and voice, and one workhorse for each checkout it works in, found by the thread a notification or tool call names
nodes.description: One record per tab session, opened when a pane socket of the tab connects and built by codex-workbench-session-factories.ts. The coordinator, voice, spoken approval, coordinator tools and callbacks are the tab's; the workhorses are built on first use, one for each checkout. A notification goes to the session that owns its thread, or to every session when no session owns the thread yet, and a workhorse thread belongs to its workhorse. A tool call from a thread that no session owns is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody. It notes the conversation shown when each coordinator turn starts and the work each workhorse's operations give. When a session ends, every link is cleared, its approvals are cancelled, its voice and board news stop, and its threads are unsubscribed once no turn runs on them.

nodes.name: Tab session presence
nodes.responsibility: Knows which browser tab each pane on screen belongs to, which checkout's conversation the tab shows, and ends a tab session when no pane of it comes back within 60 seconds
nodes.description: It lives as long as the server process, not as long as one child. A pane of the tab that comes back within the grace cancels the end, so a reload keeps the conversation. The shown checkout is pinned on the first read to the checkout of the tab's focused pane, else of the pane that asked, and only the person's own act in the page changes it, through the activation route: an agent's browser show never does, so the dock never moves while somebody types. It ends with the tab.

nodes.name: Conversation start
nodes.responsibility: Starts a conversation on a pane's first message or Talk: the tab's coordinator ready first, then the workhorse of the shown checkout, then board news to it
nodes.description: A coordinator that cannot start refuses the message or Talk with its reason, and no workhorse starts. New conversation replaces the workhorse of the shown checkout only and keeps the tab's coordinator, which speaks for every workhorse of the tab. The old workhorse thread is given up and Codex unloads it once no turn runs on it. A delegation to a checkout whose workhorse has no thread that can run turns starts that thread the same way, but leaves the coordinator alone: it is running the turn that gives the work.

nodes.name: Workhorse start
nodes.responsibility: Opens the thread one workhorse's link will name, with its instructions and both tool manifests, under a staged epoch operation
nodes.description: Start an architectural assistant with existing permissions. Its role permits inspection, diagnostics, proposals, and requested architecture documents. Carry that role into descendants. Save explicit implementation briefs in the OS temporary directory.

nodes.name: Thread unload
nodes.responsibility: Unsubscribes a thread once no turn and no voice session runs on it, so Codex unloads it
nodes.description: It reads the thread's status first, then follows the child's notifications until the thread is idle and its voice session has closed. The thread keeps its history on disk either way. The module is reached through createCodexThreadUnload from its root; the returned unload method implements this responsibility.

nodes.name: Session workhorses
nodes.responsibility: One workhorse for each checkout of a tab session: its starter, board news, queue, operations and link actions, built on first use
nodes.description: A workhorse works in its checkout, the directory that holds its vault, so it reads that repository's AGENTS.md, skills and Codex configuration. Its thread-link key is the tab session and the checkout together. It belongs to the checkout, not to the repository identity, so a new chosen checkout leaves it linked. noteActiveTurn keeps the turn running on a workhorse from turn/started on its current thread to the turn/completed of the thread the turn started on, which New conversation may have left meanwhile, and stopWorkhorses interrupts that turn for one checkout or for every workhorse of the tab. The coordinator's stop_workhorses tool stops every running workhorse of its tab session by voice.

nodes.name: Workhorse checkouts
nodes.responsibility: Names the checkout a coordinator call gives work to, and starts that checkout's workhorse when a delegation finds none
nodes.description: The checkout a path names is the directory that holds the vault the path resolves to, by real path and in the layout the server serves: a directory that holds a .archboard/vault, or the directory that holds a vault the path is. So a checkout reached through a link, and a vault that is itself a link, name the checkout of the pane in it; a vault whose link leads out of the layout names none. Of the coordinator's tools only a delegation starts a workhorse; the other three refuse a checkout that has none. A workhorse that cannot be built or started, because its tab has gone, leaves the delegation to refuse, so the coordinator's turn is always answered.

nodes.name: Workhorse list
nodes.responsibility: Lists the tab session's live workhorses by repository and checkout, with the shown one and a mark for each that waits for an approval or for the person
nodes.description: The shown checkout is listed even before its first message, as not live, because a typed message goes there. A workhorse is live once its start has a thread. The list is bounded so a snapshot always fits the browser contract, and it is read into the owner projection that every pane of the tab receives.

nodes.name: Coordinator turn homes
nodes.responsibility: Remembers, for each coordinator turn, the conversation shown when it started and the checkouts it gave work to, so the dock shows the turn in the right conversation
nodes.description: A turn that delivered, steered or queued work, or whose delivery may have reached the workhorse, shows in the conversation of each workhorse it reached. A delegation the workhorse refused as busy or with an invalid body gave it nothing, and moves the turn nowhere. A turn that gave work to none shows in the conversation shown while it ran. A turn with no record shows in whatever conversation is shown. The timeline keeps only the turns of the shown conversation before it spends its budget.

beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: A tab holds one coordinator and a workhorse for each checkout
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own lease and its own coordinator. A pane's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse of the checkout that pane shows, which that checkout's link then names. The pane that holds the lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits that thread's queue. A pane that moves to another checkout reaches the workhorse there instead. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread that works in no checkout
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It runs in a directory of its own that holds no vault, so every command it runs names its checkout with -C. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorses and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse of the checkout it names, starting that workhorse when there is none. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach each workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made goes into the history of the workhorse whose checkout holds the board, as one developer message, after the child, epoch, that workhorse's link and cursor are checked again. It starts no turn. Each delivery settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried.

beats.heading: Each thread belongs to one tab session
beats.body: The tab sessions know which session owns each thread. A notification or tool call from a thread goes to that session alone, and an approval goes to the panes of that session (a workhorse's to those of its checkout), so one tab's news and approvals never reach another tab. A notification for a thread that no session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

beats.heading: A tab session ends 60 seconds after its last pane closes
beats.body: Every pane names its tab when its socket opens. When no pane of the tab comes back for 60 seconds, the session ends: its lease and link go, its pending approvals are cancelled, voice and board news stop, and each of its threads is unsubscribed once no turn runs on it, so Codex unloads it. A reload within that time keeps the conversation and its approvals. When the child exits, every session is dropped, and a tab's next message starts a new workhorse.

nodes.name: Generation composition
nodes.responsibility: Starts the private child, then builds each generation's object graph over a transport and identity ledger that outlive it
nodes.description: installProductionCodexWorkbench hands the owner lifecycle createCodexProcess and a generation factory. The factories (codex-workbench-factories.ts) build the components in the order they depend on each other, the gateway last. codex-workbench-session-factories.ts builds one tab session's owners when the tab sessions open it. A child's exit drops every tab session, and nothing is resumed.

nodes.name: Browser gateway
nodes.responsibility: The one door a browser has into the workbench: snapshots out, with the coordinator's turns beside the workhorse's, admitted commands in, one lease per tab session, for the checkout the tab shows
nodes.description: The gateway asks which checkout the pane's tab shows on every read and command, because the person can activate another one at any time. It hears the change and presents every pane of the tab again, with the workhorse of the new checkout. A lease taken before a switch is refused as link_changed. A command runs on the workhorse its lease was claimed for, and once it has run only that workhorse's own link is asked whether it still stands, so a switch meanwhile does not make its outcome unknown. A workhorse's approval terminal is retired once the panes that show its checkout have shown it, and a coordinator's once every pane of the tab has.

nodes.name: Codex process
nodes.responsibility: Owns the child: proves the executable, prepares the Codex home every Archboard server on the machine shares, spawns the child in the coordinator's directory and reaps its group
nodes.description: One Archboard-only CODEX_HOME and SQLite home under the state directory serve every server on the machine, so one sign-in serves them all; each server keeps its own owner lock and epoch ledger under its port. Its config.toml gets the auto-review defaults it lacks (approvals_reviewer auto_review, workspace-write sandbox with network access) and keeps whatever Codex or a person set; a config naming another SQLite home, or not TOML, is refused. The child runs in the coordinator's directory under the server's state directory, which is no checkout and holds no vault, only a link to the server's archboard skill: the coordinator thread works there, so a command it runs without -C is refused, while each workhorse thread works in its own checkout. The child's environment is a short allow-list plus the server's own URL, with auto-start off and the server's bin directory first on PATH: a thread's archboard is the server's own source in whichever checkout the thread works in, and it never starts another server. On shutdown, stdin closes first. The owner waits within a short EOF grace, then reaps every remaining group within the composed deadline.

nodes.name: Codex transport
nodes.responsibility: One newline-framed JSON object at a time each way, correlated to its request, and each tool call routed to the owner registered for its namespace
nodes.description: The versioned wire contract it decodes against lives beside it in codex-protocol. A dynamic tool call reaches the owner registered for its namespace and manifest digest: the thread tools, the coordinator tools, or tell_coordinator.

So a checkout reached through a link, and a vault that is itself a link, name the checkout of the pane in it; a vault whose link leads out of the layout names none. Of the coordinator's tools only a delegation starts a workhorse; the other three refuse a checkout that has none. A workhorse that cannot be built or started, because its tab has gone, leaves the delegation to refuse, so the coordinator's turn is always answered.

nodes.name: Workhorse list
nodes.responsibility: Lists the tab session's live workhorses by repository and checkout, with the shown one and a mark for each that waits for an approval or for the person
nodes.description: The shown checkout is listed even before its first message, as not live, because a typed message goes there. A workhorse is live once its start has a thread. The list is bounded so a snapshot always fits the browser contract, and it is read into the owner projection that every pane of the tab receives.

nodes.name: Coordinator turn homes
nodes.responsibility: Remembers where each coordinator turn shows (the conversation shown when it started, the checkouts it gave work to) and which coordinator turn delegated each workhorse turn
nodes.description: A turn that delivered, steered or queued work, or whose delivery may have reached the workhorse, shows in the conversation of each workhorse it reached. A delegation the workhorse refused as busy or with an invalid body gave it nothing, and moves the turn nowhere. A turn that gave work to none shows in the conversation shown while it ran. A turn with no record shows in whatever conversation is shown. The timeline keeps only the turns of the shown conversation before it spends its budget. It also keeps which voice coordinator turn delegated each workhorse turn: a listener on the tab session's workhorse operations records a workhorse turn only from a delegate operation's event that names that turn, because a steer must not mark a turn the user began. It keeps the 256 newest records in the tab session's state. The browser gateway hands that record to the projection of the workhorse timeline, and a recorded turn then carries delegatedBy.

beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: A tab holds one coordinator and a workhorse for each checkout
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own lease and its own coordinator. A pane's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse of the checkout that pane shows, which that checkout's link then names. The pane that holds the lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits that thread's queue. A pane that moves to another checkout reaches the workhorse there instead. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread that works in no checkout
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It runs in a directory of its own that holds no vault, so every command it runs names its checkout with -C. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorses and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse of the checkout it names, starting that workhorse when there is none. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach each workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made goes into the history of the workhorse whose checkout holds the board, as one developer message, after the child, epoch, that workhorse's link and cursor are checked again. It starts no turn. Each delivery settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried.

beats.heading: Each thread belongs to one tab session
beats.body: The tab sessions know which session owns each thread. A notification or tool call from a thread goes to that session alone, and an approval goes to the panes of that session (a workhorse's to those of its checkout), so one tab's news and approvals never reach another tab. A notification for a thread that no session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

beats.heading: A tab session ends 60 seconds after its last pane closes
beats.body: Every pane names its tab when its socket opens. When no pane of the tab comes back for 60 seconds, the session ends: its lease and link go, its pending approvals are cancelled, voice and board news stop, and each of its threads is unsubscribed once no turn runs on it, so Codex unloads it. A reload within that time keeps the conversation and its approvals. When the child exits, every session is dropped, and a tab's next message starts a new workhorse.

nodes.name: Generation composition
nodes.responsibility: Starts the private child, then builds each generation's object graph over a transport and identity ledger that outlive it
nodes.description: installProductionCodexWorkbench hands the owner lifecycle createCodexProcess and a generation factory. The factories (codex-workbench-factories.ts) build the components in the order they depend on each other, the gateway last. codex-workbench-session-factories.ts builds one tab session's owners when the tab sessions open it. A child's exit drops every tab session, and nothing is resumed.

nodes.name: Browser gateway
nodes.responsibility: The one door a browser has into the workbench: snapshots out, admitted commands in, one lease per tab session, and every pane of a tab is carried out by the workhorse of the checkout the tab shows
nodes.description: The gateway asks which checkout the pane's tab shows on every read and command, because the person can activate another one at any time. It hears the change and presents every pane of the tab again, with the workhorse of the new checkout. A lease taken before a switch is refused as link_changed. A command runs on the workhorse its lease was claimed for, and once it has run only that workhorse's own link is asked whether it still stands, so a switch meanwhile does not make its outcome unknown. A workhorse's approval terminal is retired once the panes that show its checkout have shown it, and a coordinator's once every pane of the tab has.

nodes.name: Codex process
nodes.responsibility: Owns the child: proves the executable, prepares the Codex home every Archboard server on the machine shares, spawns the child in the coordinator's directory and reaps its group
nodes.description: One Archboard-only CODEX_HOME and SQLite home under the state directory serve every server on the machine, so one sign-in serves them all; each server keeps its own owner lock and epoch ledger under its port. Its config.toml gets the auto-review defaults it lacks (approvals_reviewer auto_review, workspace-write sandbox with network access) and keeps whatever Codex or a person set; a config naming another SQLite home, or not TOML, is refused. The child runs in the coordinator's directory under the server's state directory, which is no checkout and holds no vault, only a link to the server's archboard skill: the coordinator thread works there, so a command it runs without -C is refused, while each workhorse thread works in its own checkout. The child's environment is a short allow-list plus the server's own URL, with auto-start off and the server's bin directory first on PATH: a thread's archboard is the server's own source in whichever checkout the thread works in, and it never starts another server. On shutdown, stdin closes first. The owner waits within a short EOF grace, then reaps every remaining group within the composed deadline.

nodes.name: Codex transport
nodes.responsibility: One newline-framed JSON object at a time each way, correlated to its request, and each tool call routed to the owner registered for its namespace
nodes.description: The versioned wire contract it decodes against lives beside it in codex-protocol. A dynamic tool call reaches the owner registered for its namespace and manifest digest: the thread tools, the coordinator tools, or tell_coordinator.

nodes.responsibility: One initialized session and the reviewed methods it will send

nodes.name: Thread link

nodes.name: Workhorse queue

nodes.name: Voice coordinator

nodes.name: Epoch ledger

nodes.name: Workhorse operations

nodes.name: Approvals
nodes.responsibility: Every approval the child raises: staged, published to the tab session whose thread asked, answered exactly once, settled
nodes.description: An approval from a thread that no live tab session owns is cancelled when it arrives. A reload within the grace keeps a tab session's pending approvals, and the end of the session cancels them. A workhorse's approval is shown to the panes of its tab that show its checkout, and the coordinator's to every pane of its tab session.

nodes.name: Coordinator callbacks

nodes.description: Before each delivery it checks the child, epoch, thread link and cursor again; the outcome is delivered, not delivered with a reason, or unknown, and it is never retried.

nodes.name: Semantic context
nodes.responsibility: One per tab session for voice and one per workhorse for the boards of its checkout: turns the panes' gestures and every settled board change into briefs and events
nodes.description: Each brief names its board's vault, so a thread passes it to the CLI with -C. The voice side hears the board changes of the vaults its tab session's panes are in, and a workhorse hears only those of the vaults in its own checkout, so it is told about the boards it works on.

nodes.name: Tab sessions
nodes.responsibility: What each browser tab owns: its coordinator and voice, and one workhorse for each checkout it works in, found by the thread a notification or tool call names
nodes.description: One record per tab session, opened when a pane socket of the tab connects and built by codex-workbench-session-factories.ts. The coordinator, voice, spoken approval, coordinator tools and callbacks are the tab's; the workhorses are built on first use, one for each checkout. A notification goes to the session that owns its thread, or to every session when no session owns the thread yet, and a workhorse thread belongs to its workhorse. A tool call from a thread that no session owns is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody. It notes the conversation shown when each coordinator turn starts and the work each workhorse's operations give. When a session ends, every link is cleared, its approvals are cancelled, its voice and board news stop, and its threads are unsubscribed once no turn runs on them.

nodes.name: Tab session presence
nodes.responsibility: Knows which browser tab each pane on screen belongs to, which checkout's conversation the tab shows, and ends a tab session when no pane of it comes back within 60 seconds
nodes.description: It lives as long as the server process, not as long as one child. A pane of the tab that comes back within the grace cancels the end, so a reload keeps the conversation. The shown checkout is pinned on the first read to the checkout of the tab's focused pane, else of the pane that asked, and only the person's own act in the page changes it, through the activation route: an agent's browser show never does, so the dock never moves while somebody types. It ends with the tab.

nodes.name: Conversation start
nodes.responsibility: Starts a conversation on a pane's first message or Talk: the tab's coordinator ready first, then the workhorse of the shown checkout, then board news to it
nodes.description: A coordinator that cannot start refuses the message or Talk with its reason, and no workhorse starts. New conversation replaces the workhorse of the shown checkout only and keeps the tab's coordinator, which speaks for every workhorse of the tab. The old workhorse thread is given up and Codex unloads it once no turn runs on it. A delegation to a checkout whose workhorse has no thread that can run turns starts that thread the same way, but leaves the coordinator alone: it is running the turn that gives the work.

nodes.name: Workhorse start
nodes.responsibility: Opens the thread one workhorse's link will name, with its instructions and both tool manifests, under a staged epoch operation

nodes.name: Thread unload
nodes.responsibility: Unsubscribes a thread once no turn and no voice session runs on it, so Codex unloads it
nodes.description: It reads the thread's status first, then follows the child's notifications until the thread is idle and its voice session has closed. The thread keeps its history on disk either way. The module is reached through createCodexThreadUnload from its root; the returned unload method implements this responsibility.

nodes.name: Session workhorses
nodes.responsibility: One workhorse for each checkout of a tab session: its starter, board news, queue, operations and link actions, built on first use
nodes.description: A workhorse works in its checkout, the directory that holds its vault, so it reads that repository's AGENTS.md, skills and Codex configuration. Its thread-link key is the tab session and the checkout together. It belongs to the checkout, not to the repository identity, so a new chosen checkout leaves it linked. noteActiveTurn keeps the turn running on a workhorse from turn/started on its current thread to the turn/completed of the thread the turn started on, which New conversation may have left meanwhile, and stopWorkhorses interrupts that turn for one checkout or for every workhorse of the tab. The coordinator's stop_workhorses tool stops every running workhorse of its tab session by voice.

nodes.description: The checkout a path names is the directory that holds the vault the path resolves to, by real path and in the layout the server serves: a directory that holds a .archboard/vault, or the directory that holds a vault the path is. So a checkout reached through a link, and a vault that is itself a link, name the checkout of the pane in it; a vault whose link leads out of the layout names none. The list is bounded so a snapshot always fits the browser contract, and it is read into the owner projection that every pane of the tab receives.

A turn with no record shows in whatever conversation is shown. The timeline keeps only the turns of the shown conversation before it spends its budget.

beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: A tab holds one coordinator and a workhorse for each checkout
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own lease and its own coordinator. A pane's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse of the checkout that pane shows, which that checkout's link then names. The pane that holds the lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits that thread's queue. A pane that moves to another checkout reaches the workhorse there instead. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread that works in no checkout
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It runs in a directory of its own that holds no vault, so every command it runs names its checkout with -C. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorses and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse of the checkout it names, starting that workhorse when there is none. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach each workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made goes into the history of the workhorse whose checkout holds the board, as one developer message, after the child, epoch, that workhorse's link and cursor are checked again. It starts no turn. Each delivery settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried.

beats.heading: Each thread belongs to one tab session
beats.body: The tab sessions know which session owns each thread. A notification or tool call from a thread goes to that session alone, and an approval goes to the panes of that session (a workhorse's to those of its checkout), so one tab's news and approvals never reach another tab. A notification for a thread that no session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

beats.heading: A tab session ends 60 seconds after its last pane closes
beats.body: Every pane names its tab when its socket opens. When no pane of the tab comes back for 60 seconds, the session ends: its lease and link go, its pending approvals are cancelled, voice and board news stop, and each of its threads is unsubscribed once no turn runs on it, so Codex unloads it. A reload within that time keeps the conversation and its approvals. When the child exits, every session is dropped, and a tab's next message starts a new workhorse.

nodes.name: Generation composition
nodes.responsibility: Starts the private child, then builds each generation's object graph over a transport and identity ledger that outlive it
nodes.description: installProductionCodexWorkbench hands the owner lifecycle createCodexProcess and a generation factory. The factories (codex-workbench-factories.ts) build the components in the order they depend on each other, the gateway last. codex-workbench-session-factories.ts builds one tab session's owners when the tab sessions open it. A child's exit drops every tab session, and nothing is resumed.

nodes.name: Browser gateway
nodes.responsibility: The one door a browser has into the workbench: snapshots out, admitted commands in, one lease per tab session, and every pane of a tab is carried out by the workhorse of the checkout the tab shows
nodes.description: The gateway asks which checkout the pane's tab shows on every read and command, because the person can activate another one at any time. It hears the change and presents every pane of the tab again, with the workhorse of the new checkout. A lease taken before a switch is refused as link_changed. A command runs on the workhorse its lease was claimed for, and once it has run only that workhorse's own link is asked whether it still stands, so a switch meanwhile does not make its outcome unknown. A workhorse's approval terminal is retired once the panes that show its checkout have shown it, and a coordinator's once every pane of the tab has.

nodes.name: Codex process
nodes.responsibility: Owns the child: proves the executable, prepares the Codex home in the storage the host names, spawns the child in the coordinator's directory and reaps its group
nodes.description: The host names the storage. Archboard names one Archboard-only CODEX_HOME and SQLite home under the state directory, which serve every server on the machine, so one sign-in serves them all; each server keeps its own owner lock and epoch ledger under its port. Its config.toml gets the auto-review defaults it lacks (approvals_reviewer auto_review, workspace-write sandbox with network access) and keeps whatever Codex or a person set; a config naming another SQLite home, or not TOML, is refused. The child runs in the coordinator's directory under the server's state directory, which is no checkout and holds no vault, only a link to the server's archboard skill: the coordinator thread works there, so a command it runs without -C is refused, while each workhorse thread works in its own checkout. The child's environment is a short allow-list plus what the host adds. Archboard adds the server's own URL, with auto-start off, and the server's bin directory first on PATH: a thread's archboard is the server's own source in whichever checkout the thread works in, and it never starts another server. On shutdown, stdin closes first. The owner waits within a short EOF grace, then reaps every remaining group within the composed deadline.

nodes.name: Codex transport
nodes.responsibility: One newline-framed JSON object at a time each way, correlated to its request, and each tool call routed to the owner registered for its namespace
nodes.description: The versioned wire contract it decodes against lives beside it in codex-protocol. A dynamic tool call reaches the owner registered for its namespace and manifest digest: the thread tools, the coordinator tools, or tell_coordinator.

nodes.name: Codex session
nodes.responsibility: One initialized session and the reviewed methods it will send

nodes.name: Thread link
nodes.responsibility: Which workhorse each tab session and checkout is bound to, made by the first message or Talk of the pane's checkout: the binding, and the refusal when two disagree

nodes.name: Workhorse queue
nodes.responsibility: Codex's queue of messages waiting for the workhorse: list, add, edit, reorder, delete, or start one now

nodes.name: Voice coordinator
nodes.responsibility: The separate fast thread each tab session's voice attaches to, started with the tab's first message or Talk: the voice model's subconscious, which routes sustained work to a named checkout's workhorse

nodes.name: Codex app-server
nodes.responsibility: The pinned Codex binary runs as one private child over stdio in the host-owned Codex home.
nodes.description: Spawned as `app-server --stdio --strict-config`. Its threads are each tab session's coordinator and one workhorse for each checkout, and every thread runs in its auto-review mode. Nothing here describes its internals.

nodes.name: Browser pane
nodes.responsibility: The pane a user works in: it names its tab session, holds the tab's lease, sends commands and draws the published state

nodes.name: Epoch ledger
nodes.responsibility: Which child generation owns which thread, on disk, with staged operations that commit or roll back

nodes.name: Workhorse operations
nodes.responsibility: The four things the coordinator may ask of the workhorse of a checkout it names, one at a time: delegate, steer, inspect, manage its queue; each workhorse has its own

nodes.name: Realtime voice
nodes.responsibility: Starts the realtime leg on the coordinator's thread, hands a narrated walkthrough's steps to the voice model, and carries its transcript back
nodes.description: The server never speaks to a voice endpoint itself: the child brokers it, and the media travels browser to provider over the peer connection the tab made.

nodes.name: Approvals
nodes.responsibility: Every approval the child raises: staged, published to the tab session whose thread asked, answered exactly once, settled
nodes.description: An approval from a thread that no live tab session owns is cancelled when it arrives. A reload within the grace keeps a tab session's pending approvals, and the end of the session cancels them. A workhorse's approval is shown to the panes of its tab that show its checkout, and the coordinator's to every pane of its tab session.

nodes.name: Thread tool calls
nodes.responsibility: The archboard_app tools a thread calls on the server's other threads: list, read, create, fork, message, wait
nodes.description: A creation, fork or message runs only once the user approves it in a pane of the calling thread's tab session, under the generation that may act. A thread it creates or forks works in the checkout of its caller.

nodes.name: Coordinator callbacks
nodes.responsibility: While voice is live, workhorse news for the coordinator, naming the checkout of its workhorse, and pane news for the voice model, each once and in order

nodes.name: Board-change delivery
nodes.responsibility: Tells each workhorse what changed in the host's context of its checkout, in Archboard the boards a user changed: one quiet developer message, settled once
nodes.description: Before each delivery it checks the child, epoch, thread link and cursor again; the outcome is delivered, not delivered with a reason, or unknown, and it is never retried.

nodes.name: Semantic context
nodes.responsibility: One per tab session for voice and one per workhorse for the boards of its checkout: turns the panes' gestures and every settled board change into briefs and events
nodes.description: Each brief names its board's vault, so a thread passes it to the CLI with -C. The voice side hears the board changes of the vaults its tab session's panes are in, and a workhorse hears only those of the vaults in its own checkout, so it is told about the boards it works on.

nodes.name: Tab sessions
nodes.responsibility: What each browser tab owns: its coordinator and voice, and one workhorse for each checkout it works in, found by the thread a notification or tool call names
nodes.description: One record per tab session, opened when a pane socket of the tab connects and built by sessions/factories.ts. The coordinator, voice, spoken approval, coordinator tools and callbacks are the tab's; the workhorses are built on first use, one for each checkout. A notification goes to the session that owns its thread, or to every session when no session owns the thread yet, and a workhorse thread belongs to its workhorse. A tool call from a thread that no session owns is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody. It notes the conversation shown when each coordinator turn starts and the work each workhorse's operations give. When a session ends, every link is cleared, its approvals are cancelled, its voice and board news stop, and its threads are unsubscribed once no turn runs on them.

nodes.name: Tab session presence
nodes.responsibility: Knows which browser tab each pane on screen belongs to, which checkout's conversation the tab shows, and ends a tab session when no pane of it comes back within 60 seconds
nodes.description: It lives as long as the server process, not as long as one child. A pane of the tab that comes back within the grace cancels the end, so a reload keeps the conversation. The shown checkout is pinned on the first read to the checkout of the tab's focused pane, else of the pane that asked, and only the person's own act in the page changes it, through the activation route: an agent's browser show never does, so the dock never moves while somebody types. It ends with the tab.

nodes.name: Conversation start
nodes.responsibility: Starts a conversation on a pane's first message or Talk: the tab's coordinator ready first, then the workhorse of the shown checkout, then board news to it
nodes.description: A coordinator that cannot start refuses the message or Talk with its reason, and no workhorse starts. New conversation replaces the workhorse of the shown checkout only and keeps the tab's coordinator, which speaks for every workhorse of the tab. The old workhorse thread is given up and Codex unloads it once no turn runs on it. A delegation to a checkout whose workhorse has no thread that can run turns starts that thread the same way, but leaves the coordinator alone: it is running the turn that gives the work.

nodes.name: Workhorse start
nodes.responsibility: Opens the thread one workhorse's link will name, with its instructions and both tool manifests, under a staged epoch operation

nodes.name: Thread unload
nodes.responsibility: Unsubscribes a thread once no turn and no voice session runs on it, so Codex unloads it
nodes.description: It reads the thread's status first, then follows the child's notifications until the thread is idle and its voice session has closed. The thread keeps its history on disk either way. The module is reached through createCodexThreadUnload from its root; the returned unload method implements this responsibility.

nodes.name: Session workhorses
nodes.responsibility: One workhorse for each checkout of a tab session: its starter, board news, queue, operations and link actions, built on first use
nodes.description: A workhorse works in its checkout, the directory that holds its vault, so it reads that repository's AGENTS.md, skills and Codex configuration. Its thread-link key is the tab session and the checkout together. It belongs to the checkout, not to the repository identity, so a new chosen checkout leaves it linked. noteActiveTurn keeps the turn running on a workhorse from turn/started on its current thread to the turn/completed of the thread the turn started on, which New conversation may have left meanwhile, and stopWorkhorses interrupts that turn for one checkout or for every workhorse of the tab. The coordinator's stop_workhorses tool stops every running workhorse of its tab session by voice.

nodes.name: Workhorse checkouts
nodes.responsibility: Names the checkout a coordinator call gives work to, and starts that checkout's workhorse when a delegation finds none
nodes.description: The checkout a path names is the directory that holds the vault the path resolves to, by real path and in the layout the server serves: a directory that holds a .archboard/vault, or the directory that holds a vault the path is. So a checkout reached through a link, and a vault that is itself a link, name the checkout of the pane in it; a vault whose link leads out of the layout names none. Of the coordinator's tools only a delegation starts a workhorse; the other three refuse a checkout that has none. A workhorse that cannot be built or started, because its tab has gone, leaves the delegation to refuse, so the coordinator's turn is always answered.

nodes.name: Workhorse list
nodes.responsibility: Lists the tab session's live workhorses by repository and checkout, with the shown one and a mark for each that waits for an approval or for the person
nodes.description: The shown checkout is listed even before its first message, as not live, because a typed message goes there. A workhorse is live once its start has a thread. The list is bounded so a snapshot always fits the browser contract, and it is read into the owner projection that every pane of the tab receives.

nodes.name: Coordinator turn homes
nodes.responsibility: Remembers, for each coordinator turn, the conversation shown when it started and the checkouts it gave work to, so the dock shows the turn in the right conversation
nodes.description: A turn that delivered, steered or queued work, or whose delivery may have reached the workhorse, shows in the conversation of each workhorse it reached. A delegation the workhorse refused as busy or with an invalid body gave it nothing, and moves the turn nowhere. A turn that gave work to none shows in the conversation shown while it ran. A turn with no record shows in whatever conversation is shown. The timeline keeps only the turns of the shown conversation before it spends its budget.

nodes.name: Child ownership
nodes.responsibility: Owns the private Codex child and what outlives each generation of it: the process, the transport, the protocol session, the ledger of which generation owns a thread, and unloading idle threads

nodes.name: Per-tab sessions
nodes.responsibility: Gives each browser tab its own session: finds the session a call names, knows which tab each pane belongs to, ends a tab no pane returns to, and remembers where each coordinator turn is shown

nodes.name: Pane conversations
nodes.responsibility: What a pane sees and says: the gateway with its lease, snapshots and commands, the start of a conversation, the dock's list of workhorses, and the approvals raised to the person

nodes.name: Workhorses
nodes.responsibility: The sustained work of each checkout: a workhorse's thread link, queue, operations, start and board news, built per tab session on first use, with its tool calls and the context of what changed

nodes.name: Voice
nodes.responsibility: The separate fast coordinator thread of a tab session, its realtime voice leg, and the callbacks that tell it and the voice model workhorse and pane news while voice is live

nodes.name: Command admission
nodes.responsibility: Admits a command only under its live lease, link, readiness and pending approval

nodes.name: Command dispatch
nodes.responsibility: Routes each admitted command to its account, thread, text, queue, approval or voice action

nodes.name: Typed message actions
nodes.responsibility: Reads the exact leased thread and starts, steers or interrupts its turn

nodes.name: Turn execution
nodes.responsibility: Implements delegation, steering, inspection and queue changes through the shared operation runtime

nodes.name: Operation validation
nodes.responsibility: Captures the current binding and classifies both linked threads around each coordinator effect

nodes.name: Operation lifecycle
nodes.responsibility: Stages operations, follows their workhorse turns and settles their outcomes once

nodes.name: Operations contract
nodes.responsibility: Defines the requests, results and notifications of the four workhorse operations

nodes.name: Start contract
nodes.responsibility: Defines the starter port that exposes thread creation and its current snapshot

nodes.name: Browser message publication
nodes.responsibility: Delivers each gateway update to its connection subscribers without one failed listener blocking the others

nodes.name: Application policy
nodes.responsibility: Archboard's options for the voice agent: its identity and tool names, domain instructions, context, tools, storage, Codex environment and admitted checkouts

nodes.name: Workbench interface
nodes.responsibility: Starts the shared Codex sessions the voice agent asks for and owns their connections, lifecycle, and state through one host contract

nodes.name: Archboard tab adapter
nodes.responsibility: Forward pane registration and browser activation to core-owned tab state

nodes.name: Voice agent
nodes.responsibility: The host's one entry: createVoiceAgent turns its storage, Codex, checkouts, instructions, identity and extensions into one workbench, and serves its browser sockets on node:http or Bun.serve
nodes.description: start, status, shutdown and the browser port come from the workbench it creates. attach admits sockets on one path of a node:http server, and bunHandlers wraps the fetch and websocket handlers of Bun.serve; both admit an upgrade only from the one origin and on the one path the host names, and work in the checkout the host names for that path. The role profiles are composed here from the host's instructions, tools and identity, so every thread Codex is given carries the host's names and no other.

nodes.name: Voice client
nodes.responsibility: The package's browser client for a host page: one socket on the host's path with its tab session, one frozen state and the page's actions, and a new socket after a lost one
nodes.description: createVoiceClient owns the socket, the tab session id, the transport and media owners and the state a page draws; an uncertain delivery stays visible as a failure. ./react reads it through VoiceClientProvider, useVoiceClient and useVoiceState. A host that owns its sockets, as Archboard does, builds on ./controllers instead.

nodes.name: Example host
nodes.responsibility: A host outside Archboard on Bun.serve: one voice agent for its own checkout, its sockets through bunHandlers, and a React page on the voice client

nodes.name: Hosts
nodes.responsibility: The applications that use the package: Archboard's server policy and browser pane, and the example host
nodes.description: Archboard's adapters that plug into one mechanism of the package, as its thread tools, board context and tab adapter do, sit with that mechanism instead.

beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares the Codex home in the storage the host names. Archboard names an Archboard-only home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: A tab holds one coordinator and a workhorse for each checkout
beats.body: Each browser tab is a tab session with its own lease and its own coordinator. A pane's first message or Talk starts its conversation: the coordinator first, then the workhorse of the checkout that pane shows, which that checkout's link then names. The pane that holds the lease sends its typed message straight to that workhorse as a turn or a steer, and edits that thread's queue. A pane that moves to another checkout reaches the workhorse there instead. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread that works in no checkout
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It runs in a directory of its own that holds no vault, so every command it runs names its checkout with -C. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorses and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse of the checkout it names, starting that workhorse when there is none. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach each workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made goes into the history of the workhorse whose checkout holds the board, as one developer message, after the child, epoch, that workhorse's link and cursor are checked again. It starts no turn. Each delivery settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried.

beats.heading: Each thread belongs to one tab session
beats.body: The tab sessions know which session owns each thread. A notification or tool call from a thread goes to that session alone, and an approval goes to the panes of that session (a workhorse's to those of its checkout), so one tab's news and approvals never reach another tab. A notification for a thread that no session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

beats.heading: A tab session ends 60 seconds after its last pane closes
beats.body: Every pane names its tab when its socket opens. When no pane of the tab comes back for 60 seconds, the session ends: its lease and link go, its pending approvals are cancelled, voice and board news stop, and each of its threads is unsubscribed once no turn runs on it, so Codex unloads it. A reload within that time keeps the conversation and its approvals. When the child exits, every session is dropped, and a tab's next message starts a new workhorse.

variants.name: TASK-530.05
variants.summary: The codex-realtime-voice package as a host uses it: its entry point and browser client, the shared Codex child, tab sessions and the context changes announced to them, checkout workhorses and voice, and the Archboard and example hosts

nodes.name: Generation composition
nodes.responsibility: Starts the private child, then builds each generation's object graph over a transport and identity ledger that outlive it
nodes.description: installProductionCodexWorkbench hands the owner lifecycle createCodexProcess and a generation factory. The factories (codex-workbench-factories.ts) build the components in the order they depend on each other, the gateway last. codex-workbench-session-factories.ts builds one tab session's owners when the tab sessions open it. A child's exit drops every tab session, and nothing is resumed.

nodes.name: Browser gateway
nodes.responsibility: The one door a browser has into the workbench: snapshots out, admitted commands in, one lease per tab session, and every chat of a tab is carried out by the workhorse of the checkout the tab shows
nodes.description: The gateway asks which checkout the chat's tab shows on every read and command, because the person can activate another one at any time. It hears the change and presents every chat of the tab again, with the workhorse of the new checkout. A lease taken before a switch is refused as link_changed. A command runs on the workhorse its lease was claimed for, and once it has run only that workhorse's own link is asked whether it still stands, so a switch meanwhile does not make its outcome unknown. A workhorse's approval terminal is retired once the chats that show its checkout have shown it, and a coordinator's once every chat of the tab has.

nodes.name: Codex process
nodes.responsibility: Owns the child: proves the executable, prepares the Codex home in the storage the host names, spawns the child in the coordinator's directory and reaps its group
nodes.description: The host names the storage. Archboard names one Archboard-only CODEX_HOME and SQLite home under the state directory, which serve every server on the machine, so one sign-in serves them all; each server keeps its own owner lock and epoch ledger under its port. Its config.toml gets the auto-review defaults it lacks (approvals_reviewer auto_review, workspace-write sandbox with network access) and keeps whatever Codex or a person set; a config naming another SQLite home, or not TOML, is refused. The child runs in the coordinator's directory under the server's state directory, which is no checkout and holds no vault, only a link to the server's archboard skill: the coordinator thread works there, so a command it runs without -C is refused, while each workhorse thread works in its own checkout. The child's environment is a short allow-list plus what the host adds. Archboard adds the server's own URL, with auto-start off, and the server's bin directory first on PATH: a thread's archboard is the server's own source in whichever checkout the thread works in, and it never starts another server. On shutdown, stdin closes first. The owner waits within a short EOF grace, then reaps every remaining group within the composed deadline.

nodes.name: Codex transport
nodes.responsibility: One newline-framed JSON object at a time each way, correlated to its request, and each tool call routed to the owner registered for its namespace
nodes.description: The versioned wire contract it decodes against lives beside it in codex-protocol. A dynamic tool call reaches the owner registered for its namespace and manifest digest: the thread tools, the coordinator tools, or tell_coordinator.

nodes.name: Codex session
nodes.responsibility: One initialized session and the reviewed methods it will send

nodes.name: Thread link
nodes.responsibility: Which workhorse each tab session and checkout is bound to, under its link key, made by the first message or Talk in that checkout: the binding, and the refusal when two disagree

nodes.name: Workhorse queue
nodes.responsibility: Codex's queue of messages waiting for the workhorse: list, add, edit, reorder, delete, or start one now

nodes.name: Voice coordinator
nodes.responsibility: The separate fast thread each tab session's voice attaches to, started with the tab's first message or Talk: the voice model's subconscious, which routes sustained work to a named checkout's workhorse

nodes.name: Codex app-server
nodes.responsibility: The pinned Codex binary runs as one private child over stdio in the host-owned Codex home.
nodes.description: Spawned as `app-server --stdio --strict-config`. Its threads are each tab session's coordinator and one workhorse for each checkout, and every thread runs in its auto-review mode. Nothing here describes its internals.

nodes.name: Browser pane
nodes.responsibility: The pane a user works in: it names its tab session, holds the tab's lease, sends commands and draws the published state

nodes.name: Epoch ledger
nodes.responsibility: Which child generation owns which thread, on disk, with staged operations that commit or roll back

nodes.name: Workhorse operations
nodes.responsibility: The four things the coordinator may ask of the workhorse of a checkout it names, one at a time: delegate, steer, inspect, manage its queue; each workhorse has its own

nodes.name: Realtime voice
nodes.responsibility: Starts the realtime leg on the coordinator's thread, ordinary or for a host's narrative, passes the host voice policy's input to the voice model, and carries its transcript back
nodes.description: The server never speaks to a voice endpoint itself: the child brokers it, and the media travels browser to provider over the peer connection the tab made.

nodes.name: Approvals
nodes.responsibility: Every approval the child raises: staged, published to the tab session whose thread asked, answered exactly once, settled
nodes.description: An approval from a thread that no live tab session owns is cancelled when it arrives. A reload within the grace keeps a tab session's pending approvals, and the end of the session cancels them. A workhorse's approval is shown to the chats of its tab that show its checkout, and the coordinator's to every chat of its tab session.

nodes.name: Thread tool calls
nodes.responsibility: The archboard_app tools a thread calls on the server's other threads: list, read, create, fork, message, wait
nodes.description: A creation, fork or message runs only once the user approves it in a pane of the calling thread's tab session, under the generation that may act. A thread it creates or forks works in the checkout of its caller.

nodes.name: Coordinator callbacks
nodes.responsibility: While voice is live, workhorse news for the coordinator, naming the checkout of its workhorse, and a host's context changes for the coordinator or the voice model, in order through the tab's one queue

nodes.name: Context delivery
nodes.responsibility: Tells one workhorse each context change a host announces for its checkout: one quiet developer message, settled once
nodes.description: It hears one feed's sequence at most once and refuses a sequence that does not pass the last of its feed. A change the workhorse or its tab's coordinator made is not told, nor one that went stale or whose words the host withheld. Before the write it checks the child, epoch, thread link and freshness again; the outcome is delivered, not delivered with a reason, or unknown, and it is never retried.

nodes.name: Semantic context
nodes.responsibility: One per tab session: turns its panes' gestures and every settled change of the boards in its panes' vaults into briefs and events
nodes.description: Each brief names its board's vault, so a thread passes it to the CLI with -C. It hears the board changes of the vaults its tab session's panes are in, and drops a cosmetic one, which is no news. Archboard's announcements tell each change only to the workhorse of the board's checkout, so a workhorse is told about the boards it works on.

nodes.name: Tab sessions
nodes.responsibility: What each browser tab owns: its coordinator and voice, and one workhorse for each checkout it works in, found by the thread a notification or tool call names
nodes.description: One record per tab session, opened when a chat socket of the tab connects and built by sessions/factories.ts. The coordinator, voice, spoken approval, coordinator tools and callbacks are the tab's; the workhorses are built on first use, one for each checkout. A notification goes to the session that owns its thread, or to every session when no session owns the thread yet, and a workhorse thread belongs to its workhorse. A tool call from a thread that no session owns is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody. It notes the conversation shown when each coordinator turn starts and the work each workhorse's operations give. When a session ends, every link is cleared, its approvals are cancelled, its voice and context delivery stop, and its threads are unsubscribed once no turn runs on them.

nodes.name: Tab session presence
nodes.responsibility: Knows which browser tab each chat on screen belongs to, which checkout's conversation the tab shows, and ends a tab session when no chat of it comes back within 60 seconds
nodes.description: It lives as long as the server process, not as long as one child. A chat of the tab that comes back within the grace cancels the end, so a reload keeps the conversation. A tab that shows no checkout yet is pinned on the first read to the checkout the asker names, and only the person's own act in the page changes it, through the host's activation. In Archboard the pin is the checkout of the tab's focused pane, else of the pane that asked, and an agent's browser show never moves it, so the dock never moves while somebody types. It ends with the tab.

nodes.name: Conversation start
nodes.responsibility: Starts a conversation on a chat's first message or Talk: the tab's coordinator ready first, then the workhorse of the shown checkout, then its context delivery bound to it
nodes.description: A coordinator that cannot start refuses the message or Talk with its reason, and no workhorse starts. New conversation replaces the workhorse of the shown checkout only and keeps the tab's coordinator, which speaks for every workhorse of the tab. The old workhorse thread is given up and Codex unloads it once no turn runs on it. A delegation to a checkout whose workhorse has no thread that can run turns starts that thread the same way, but leaves the coordinator alone: it is running the turn that gives the work.

nodes.name: Workhorse start
nodes.responsibility: Opens the thread one workhorse's link will name, with its instructions and both tool manifests, under a staged epoch operation

nodes.name: Thread unload
nodes.responsibility: Unsubscribes a thread once no turn and no voice session runs on it, so Codex unloads it
nodes.description: It reads the thread's status first, then follows the child's notifications until the thread is idle and its voice session has closed. The thread keeps its history on disk either way. The module is reached through createCodexThreadUnload from its root; the returned unload method implements this responsibility.

nodes.name: Session workhorses
nodes.responsibility: One workhorse for each checkout of a tab session: its starter, context delivery, queue, operations and link actions, built on first use
nodes.description: A workhorse works in its checkout, a directory the host admitted, so it reads that repository's AGENTS.md, skills and Codex configuration. Its thread-link key is the tab session and the checkout together. It belongs to the checkout, so it stays linked until its tab session ends. noteActiveTurn keeps the turn running on a workhorse from turn/started on its current thread to the turn/completed of the thread the turn started on, which New conversation may have left meanwhile, and stopWorkhorses interrupts that turn for one checkout or for every workhorse of the tab. The coordinator's stop_workhorses tool stops every running workhorse of its tab session by voice.

nodes.name: Workhorse checkouts
nodes.responsibility: Names the checkout a coordinator call gives work to, and starts that checkout's workhorse when a delegation finds none
nodes.description: A path names a checkout only when the host's resolveCheckout admits it, spelled as a real path, so a checkout reached through a link is the same checkout. Archboard admits the directory that holds the vault the path resolves to, in the layout its server serves: a directory that holds a .archboard/vault, or the directory that holds a vault the path is. Of the coordinator's tools only a delegation starts a workhorse; the other three refuse a checkout that has none. A workhorse that cannot be built or started, because its tab has gone, leaves the delegation to refuse, so the coordinator's turn is always answered.

nodes.name: Workhorse list
nodes.responsibility: Lists the tab session's live workhorses by label and checkout, with the shown one and a mark for each that waits for an approval or for the person
nodes.description: The shown checkout is listed even before its first message, as not live, because a typed message goes there. A workhorse is live once its start has a thread. The list is bounded so a snapshot always fits the browser contract, and it is read into the owner projection that every chat of the tab receives. The label is the host's checkoutLabel, by default the name of the checkout's directory; Archboard labels a checkout by the repository of the vault it holds.

nodes.name: Coordinator turn homes
nodes.responsibility: Remembers, for each coordinator turn, the conversation shown when it started and the checkouts it gave work to, so the page shows the turn in the right conversation
nodes.description: A turn that delivered, steered or queued work, or whose delivery may have reached the workhorse, shows in the conversation of each workhorse it reached. A delegation the workhorse refused as busy or with an invalid body gave it nothing, and moves the turn nowhere. A turn that gave work to none shows in the conversation shown while it ran. A turn with no record shows in whatever conversation is shown. The timeline keeps only the turns of the shown conversation before it spends its budget.

nodes.name: Child ownership
nodes.responsibility: Owns the private Codex child and what outlives each generation of it: the process, the transport, the protocol session, the ledger of which generation owns a thread, and unloading idle threads

nodes.name: Per-tab sessions
nodes.responsibility: Gives each browser tab its own session: finds the one a call names, knows each chat's tab, ends a tab no chat returns to, records where each coordinator turn shows, and announces context changes

nodes.name: Chat conversations
nodes.responsibility: What a chat sees and says: the gateway with its lease, snapshots and commands, the start of a conversation, the list of the tab's workhorses, and the approvals raised to the person

nodes.name: Workhorses
nodes.responsibility: The sustained work of each checkout: a workhorse's thread link, queue, operations, start and context delivery, built per tab session on first use, with its tool calls

nodes.name: Voice
nodes.responsibility: The separate fast coordinator thread of a tab session, its realtime voice leg, and the callbacks that tell it and the voice model workhorse news and context changes while voice is live

nodes.name: Command admission
nodes.responsibility: Admits a command only under its live lease, link, readiness and pending approval

nodes.name: Command dispatch
nodes.responsibility: Routes each admitted command to its account, thread, text, queue, approval or voice action

nodes.name: Typed message actions
nodes.responsibility: Reads the exact leased thread and starts, steers or interrupts its turn

nodes.name: Turn execution
nodes.responsibility: Implements delegation, steering, inspection and queue changes through the shared operation runtime

nodes.name: Operation validation
nodes.responsibility: Captures the current binding and classifies both linked threads around each coordinator effect

nodes.name: Operation lifecycle
nodes.responsibility: Stages operations, follows their workhorse turns and settles their outcomes once

nodes.name: Operations contract
nodes.responsibility: Defines the requests, results and notifications of the four workhorse operations

nodes.name: Start contract
nodes.responsibility: Defines the starter port that exposes thread creation and its current snapshot

nodes.name: Browser message publication
nodes.responsibility: Delivers each gateway update to its connection subscribers without one failed listener blocking the others

nodes.name: Application policy
nodes.responsibility: Archboard's options for the voice agent: identity and tool names, domain instructions, context, tools, storage, Codex environment, admitted checkouts and their labels, and its context announcer

nodes.name: Workbench interface
nodes.responsibility: Starts the shared Codex sessions the voice agent asks for and owns their connections, lifecycle, and state through one host contract, and hands each announced change to the live generation

nodes.name: Archboard tab adapter
nodes.responsibility: Forward pane registration and browser activation to core-owned tab state

nodes.name: Voice agent
nodes.responsibility: The host's one entry: createVoiceAgent turns its storage, Codex, checkouts, instructions, identity and extensions into one workbench, serves sockets on node:http or Bun.serve, and announces changes
nodes.description: start, status, shutdown and the browser port come from the workbench it creates. attach admits sockets on one path of a node:http server, and bunHandlers wraps the fetch and websocket handlers of Bun.serve; both admit an upgrade only from the one origin and on the one path the host names, and work in the checkout the host names for that path. The role profiles are composed here from the host's instructions, tools and identity, so every thread Codex is given carries the host's names and no other.

nodes.name: Voice client
nodes.responsibility: The package's browser client for a host page: one socket on the host's path with its tab session, one frozen state and the page's actions, and a new socket after a lost one
nodes.description: createVoiceClient owns the socket, the tab session id, the transport and media owners and the state a page draws; an uncertain delivery stays visible as a failure. ./react reads it through VoiceClientProvider, useVoiceClient and useVoiceState. A host that owns its sockets, as Archboard does, builds on ./controllers instead.

nodes.name: Example host
nodes.responsibility: A host outside Archboard on Bun.serve: one voice agent for its own checkout, its sockets through bunHandlers, and a React page on the voice client

nodes.name: Hosts
nodes.responsibility: The applications that use the package: Archboard's server policy and browser pane, and the example host
nodes.description: Archboard's adapters that plug into one mechanism of the package, as its thread tools, board context, announcements and tab adapter do, sit with that mechanism instead.

nodes.name: Public entries
nodes.responsibility: What a host imports: the voice agent from ./server and the voice client a page builds on

nodes.name: Context announcements
nodes.responsibility: Tells the live tab sessions a context change a host announces, each audience it names: the workhorse of each named checkout, the coordinator and the live voice, with one receipt for each
nodes.description: VoiceAgent.announce is its entry. It refuses a malformed change before anybody is told, and reads every identity itself: each told workhorse's link, child and threads, and the coordinator paired with it. A workhorse hears the change through its own context delivery, and a tab with no workhorse in a named checkout answers no_workhorse. The coordinator and the voice hear it through the tab's one callback queue, and only while voice is live: with none, the receipt says voice_inactive. The audiences are told at the same time, in no fixed order.

nodes.name: Archboard announcements
nodes.responsibility: Archboard's context changes as the voice agent announces them: each settled board change, and each focus or selection a pane reports
nodes.description: It keeps one Semantic context publisher per tab session and announces each event it publishes. A settled change's brief goes to the workhorse of the board's checkout, withheld once the brief is stale. The voice hears the news of a board on screen, as speech when it stops the narration, and nothing of a board no pane shows. The coordinator hears only what an agent outside the session did. A focus or selection the user made carries a topic, so a later one replaces it while it waits.

edges.label: start a generation
spawn the child in the coordinator directory
one JSON-RPC request per method
JSON-RPC over stdio

the link of this tab session and the shown checkout
edges.description: readWorkhorseBinding derives the workhorse key, then calls options.threadLink.read(key). The key helper does not read the link.

edges.label: a typed message: turn/start or turn/steer
lease, commands, snapshots
bind the gateway to this generation

edges.description: publishConnection emits the changed delta to connection listeners, or a replacement snapshot when the delta exceeds the wire budget. The socket subscriber carries these messages to the pane.
